title: TEFCA XP Implementation SOP: Individual Access Services (IAS) v3.0 -- MUST layer (UNOFFICIAL)
description: Unofficial profile of the generic OIDC schema (urn:x-oidc:core-1.0:schema) derived from SOP-IAS-XP-v3 (effective 2026-08-03). PRECEDENCE: requirements are cumulative where compatible. The IAS SOP defines IAS-specific content; QTF is inherited via IAS §4.2(a) and the Facilitated FHIR SOP / SSRAA via IAS §4.2(b); IAS §4.2(b) explicitly supersedes the Facilitated FHIR deadlines for IAS FHIR endpoints. Genuine conflicts are marked unresolved-conflict. Holds only MUST/SHALL/REQUIRED constraints; SHOULD/RECOMMENDED items are in urn:x-tefca-ias-sop:3.0:recommended. Load all three files together. Custom annotation keywords: x-precedence, one of: inherited (a base rule applying unchanged, e.g. QTF via IAS §4.2(a) or Facilitated FHIR/SSRAA via IAS §4.2(b)); profile-tightened (a compatible narrowing of a base rule; satisfying the profile satisfies both); explicit-override (a source text expressly replaces a base rule); superseded (an explicitly replaced deadline); unresolved-conflict (incompatible texts with no override; needs governing-priority interpretation or RCE clarification). Requirements are cumulative where compatible; genuine conflicts are never resolved by picking the apparently stricter rule. x-obligation (REQUIRED, MUST, SHALL, CONDITIONAL, MUST-IF-VERIFIED, MUST-ONE-OF, SHOULD, RECOMMENDED, MAY, OPTIONAL) and x-source (spec section). Draft 2020-12 validators collect unknown keywords as annotations; Ajv strict mode needs ajv.addKeyword() for each, or strict:false. x-not-expressible lists rules of that definition no JSON Schema can enforce. QHIN Compliance Bulletin No. 2 (toolkit 1.5.0): idTokenClaims is the SOP-text reading; idTokenClaimsCore holds the constraints it shares with urn:x-tefca-qhin-bulletin-2:1.0:schema, which replaces idTokenClaims from the Bulletin's issue date (October 13, 2026).

oidUrn.x-source: RFC 3061; RFC 8141 §3.1; IAS SOP v3.0 Table 2 + footnote 13
oidUrn.description: An OID URN. The 'urn' scheme and the 'oid' NID are case-insensitive (RFC 8141 §3.1; RFC 3061's own example is URN:OID:0.9.2342.19200300.100.4); the OID itself has no leading zeros. The lower-case form required by the FHIR oid data type, which the RCE IAS workgroup recommends (October 22, 2026), is checked in the SHOULD layer.

iso3166Alpha2.x-source: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 (249 assigned codes); IAS SOP v3.0 Table 3; RCE IAS workgroup clarification, October 22, 2026
iso3166Alpha2.description: Upper-case ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code (e.g. US). IAS Table 3 says 'Country code based on the 2-letter codes defined in ISO 3166-2'; the RCE IAS workgroup (October 22, 2026) clarified ISO 3166-1 alpha-2. Reserved codes such as UK (use GB) are not assigned codes.

region.description: 2-letter subdivision part of the ISO 3166-2 code, without the country prefix (CA from US-CA), upper case; for US addresses one of the 57 ISO 3166-2:US codes (RCE IAS workgroup clarification, October 22, 2026).

country.x-source: IAS SOP v3.0 Table 3; ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 (RCE IAS workgroup clarification, October 22, 2026)

x-not-expressible: RS256 signature validity against the CSP JWKS (§4.9(a)(ii))
aud equals the receiving IAS Provider's own HCID (Table 2 footnote 13)
claims were actually verified by the CSP (§4.9(a)(iii)) beyond *_verified flags
MUST-IF-VERIFIED claims present whenever the CSP verified them (Table 2)
csp_issued_identifier stable over time and SHOULD be unique across the CSP's clients (§4.9(a)(v))
token present in every PD, DQ, DR and FHIR auth request (§4.4(f), §4.9(d))
XCPD body carries all verified demographics (§4.4(e)); Demographics Double-Check (§4.7)
ENCOURAGED (footnote 2): CSPs that verify historical addresses, extra emails/phones, CSP identifiers

sub.x-source: IAS SOP v3.0 §4.9(a)(iii) via OIDC Core §2

aud.description: Value form is set by idTokenClaims (SOP-text reading) or by the Bulletin 2 layer (urn:x-tefca-qhin-bulletin-2:1.0:schema).

birthdate.description: All three elements present; partial dates SHALL NOT be used.

historical_address.description: Form is set by idTokenClaims (one object) or by the Bulletin 2 layer (object or array of objects).

email_verified.description: Allowed values are set by idTokenClaims (true only) or by the Bulletin 2 layer (§3).

phone_number_verified.description: Allowed values are set by idTokenClaims (true only) or by the Bulletin 2 layer (§3).

tefca_ial2claims_version.x-obligation: MUST (production decision; QHIN Compliance Bulletin No. 2 §2(a))
tefca_ial2claims_version.x-source: IAS SOP v3.0 §4.9(a)(iv), §4.8 (IAL2 Claims Tokens, October 1, 2026); implementation-group production decision; QHIN Compliance Bulletin No. 2 §2(a) (issued October 13, 2026)
tefca_ial2claims_version.description: Required, with the string value '3.0'. The SOP text makes the claim a SHOULD and defaults an omitted claim to '1.0' (§4.9(a)(iv)); the implementation group decided for production, keyed to the §4.8 date of October 1, 2026, that every IAL2 Claims Token carries '3.0', and Bulletin 2 §2(a) now requires it ('Every IAL2 Claims Token issued based on the IAS SOP v3.0 SHALL include the tefca_ial2claims_version claim with the string value “3.0”'). No 'default' keyword: validators that inject defaults would insert '1.0' and then fail the const.
tefca_ial2claims_version.x-precedence: explicit-override (Bulletin 2 §1(b), §2(a): SHOULD becomes SHALL with the value '3.0')

idTokenClaimsCore.description: Constraints shared by the SOP-text reading (#/$defs/idTokenClaims) and the QHIN Compliance Bulletin No. 2 reading (urn:x-tefca-qhin-bulletin-2:1.0:schema#/$defs/idTokenClaims). Not a complete profile on its own: aud, historical_address, the *_verified flags and the email/phone rule are set by one of those two definitions.

idTokenClaims.description: SOP-text reading of IAS SOP v3.0 without QHIN Compliance Bulletin No. 2: aud one string, historical_address one object, *_verified flags true only. ias_sop_checker uses it with --bulletin2 off or an evaluation date before 2026-10-13. From the Bulletin's issue date (October 13, 2026) the Bulletin 2 layer governs where the SOP is ambiguous or in conflict (Bulletin §1(b)).

aud.description: A single JSON string: the IAS Provider HCID as urn:oid:<oid>. Table 2 says aud MUST be the unique HCID of the IAS Provider's Directory Entry; an array (permitted by generic OIDC Core §2) is not that value.
aud.x-precedence: profile-tightened (IAS Table 2 / footnote 13 narrow OIDC's string-or-array aud to one HCID string)

historical_address.description: Same format as 'address': a single JSON object (Table 2 and Table 3). An array is not that format. Footnote 2 encourages verifying 'historical addresses' (plural), but the SOP defines no multi-address representation: open question.

idTokenClaimsStrict.description: Rejects claims not defined by OIDC, named by the SOP, or RCE-namespaced.

tefcaIasExtension.$comment: IAS §4.9(e): id_token element inside the TEFCA_IAS extension. Structure per FF SOP v2.0 Table 4 (applies via IAS §4.2(b)); token CONTENT governed by IAS §4.9 (FF Table 4 defers to the IAS SOP).
tefcaIasExtension.x-precedence: inherited via IAS §4.2(b) (structure: FF Table 4); profile-tightened by IAS (id_token content per §4.9)

id_token.description: Client-side MUST under the IAS SOP (FF only says servers SHOULD reject if missing).
id_token.x-precedence: profile-tightened (IAS client MUST is compatible with FF's server-side SHOULD)

iasHl7B2b.$comment: hl7-b2b object used for IAS client-credentials requests
iasHl7B2b.x-precedence: profile-tightened (IAS §4.1 fixes the XP value); structure inherited via IAS §4.2(b) (FF Table 2, SSRAA §5.2.1.1)

purpose_of_use.x-source: IAS SOP v3.0 §4.1 + FF Table 2 + FF §6.4
purpose_of_use.description: Exactly one code, T-IAS (bare, or system#code with the XP code system OID).

iasClientCredentialsAssertion.$comment: UDAP Authentication JWT claims for an IAS client-credentials token request
